root_cause_criterion.criterion: When the unknown-type ExtensionObject path stores the decoded `typeId` into `dst->content.encoded.typeId`, it must preserve independent ownership by copying the string-backed NodeId instead of aliasing `binTypeId`'s buffer; otherwise the later `UA_NodeId_deleteMembers(&binTypeId)` cleanup frees the same buffer still referenced by `dst->content.encoded.typeId`.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original shallow-copies the string-backed NodeId, so `dst->content.encoded.typeId.identifier.string.data` aliases `typeId->identifier.string.data`. The fixed original reaches the same source site but uses `UA_NodeId_copy(...)`, leaving the destination with distinct storage before the same cleanup executes.

nodes.state: Immediately after `UA_NodeId_deleteMembers(&binTypeId)` returns on the BYTESTRING decode-error path, `dst->content.encoded.typeId.identifier.string.data` still equals `binTypeId.identifier.string.data`, so the partially decoded ExtensionObject carries a dangling alias to the just-freed string buffer.
Outer cleanup later reaches `String_deleteMembers()` on the stale encoded NodeId and passes the same tracked string pointer as `s->data`, becoming the AddressSanitizer-reported second free.

edges.relation: The same destination string pointer stored at the unknown-type copy site remains in `dst->content.encoded.typeId` after `UA_NodeId_deleteMembers(&binTypeId)` returns.
The dangling encoded-typeId string pointer left in `dst` after `binTypeId` cleanup is later forwarded to `String_deleteMembers()` as `s->data`, where the same buffer is freed again.
